text: ,14 Acetylcysteine has also been reported to be of benefit in Raynaud’s syndrome.6,14 Cardiac involvement may be underdiagnosed;8 ACE in- hibitors or digoxin may be used.1 • Lung fibrosis is usually treated with cyclophospha- mide,1,3,5,8,15 with or without a corticosteroid such as prednisolone. There is no evidence for corticosteroids alone in lung scleroderma, and high dose may precipi- tate scleroderma renal crisis, leading to irreversible re- nal failure.7 As mentioned above, interferon gamma is under investigation. • In patients with gastrointestinal disease, proton pump inhibitors such as omeprazole, sometimes with proki- netic drugs, are extremely effective for oesophageal in- volvement, and broad spectrum antibacterials are help- ful for small bowel bacterial overgrowth.1,8 NSAIDs and corticosteroids must be used with care in scleroderma because of the risk of exacerbating renal and other problems.1,8 1.
